questions.q: Per this lesson, what's the key difference between a syntax error and a data-model error in a query?
options: A syntax error is more dangerous because it corrupts data
A syntax error fails loudly and is noticed immediately; a data-model error runs fine and returns a real but wrong-meaning result
A data-model error always crashes the Salesforce org
There is no real difference between them
questions.explain: A data-model error is more dangerous precisely because it doesn't announce itself — the query succeeds and looks plausible.

questions.q: In the double-counting example, why does joining Account to Opportunity through Contact produce a wrong pipeline total?
options: Because an Opportunity gets counted once for every Contact linked to that Account, inflating the total
Because Accounts can never have more than one Contact
Because Contacts and Opportunities are actually the same object
Because Opportunities are deleted when Contacts are added
questions.explain: Joining through Contact multiplies each Opportunity by however many Contacts exist on that Account, rather than counting it once.

questions.q: What would the correct relationship path be for a "total pipeline value per Account" query, per this lesson?
options: There is no correct path; the number can't be calculated
Opportunity joined to itself
Contact joined directly to Opportunity, without involving Account at all
Account joined directly to Opportunity, without routing through Contact
questions.explain: The lesson states the correct path is Account to Opportunity directly, not through Contact.

questions.q: Why does this course teach Chapters 2 through 6 on objects and relationships before teaching SOQL syntax in depth?
options: There's no stated reason; it's an arbitrary ordering
Because Salesforce doesn't actually support a query language
Because SOQL syntax is too difficult to teach to beginners
Because understanding objects and how they connect lets an analyst catch bad joins that query syntax alone can't prevent
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames data-model understanding as a prerequisite that prevents silent, syntax-valid errors like double-counting.

questions.q: What does this lesson mean by a query "failing silently"?
options: The query returns no rows at all
The Salesforce org crashes without any error message
The query runs successfully and returns a real, correctly formatted number that doesn't mean what the analyst assumed
The query throws a visible error message that halts execution
questions.explain: A silent failure looks like success — a real result, formatted correctly — while still being conceptually wrong.
